en: What the integration executor raises the trunk's version to when it lands a head (ADR 0134): the version the trunk declares, how far the head moves the public contract measured against the trunk's committed registry, what that movement requires under the version's mode, the repository's floor from `release.floor` in the policy, the exemption class that lowered the floor if every changed path falls in one, the larger of the requirement and the floor, and the trunk's version raised by it — with one sentence per step. Everything is read from git at the two refs, so the answer does not depend on which executable runs or on the branch's own version, which is why a retried landing cannot raise twice. It decides and writes nothing; an input that cannot be read is refused rather than guessed.

Vše se čte z gitu na dvou refech, takže odpověď nezávisí na tom, který spustitelný soubor běží, ani na vlastní verzi větve, a proto opakované přistání nemůže zvýšit dvakrát. en: Repository content is untrusted input: symlinks are never followed or read; a file over 4 MiB or a front matter over 64 KiB is refused; invalid UTF-8 is refused; only paths the declared pathspecs match are read, and only from the repository root; <t1/> and <t2/> answer from the in-memory index and the registry (one resolution of a URI, shared by both; <t3/> executes <t4/>), never from a path a client names; the HTTP server binds loopback by default, reads at most 1 MiB of body, and trusts no header beyond the session id it issued itself, which names a session and grants nothing (every session sees the same read-only registry). The lease is trusted only after the server it names has answered for this root; a peer's announcement is text other peers read, never a path the server opens. Not defended against: a hostile <t5/> naming a huge tree (the walk is bounded by the repository, not by a budget), and memory, since every object's content is held for the session.

Zápůjčce se věří, až když server, který pojmenovává, odpověděl za tento kořen; oznámení peera je text, který čtou jiní peeři, nikdy cesta, kterou server otevře. en: The registry is the part that pays for itself. Every operation is declared once, in Rust, with its identity, its effect and its exposure. As this page is built, that registry holds 2646 capabilities: 196 of them are exposed as MCP tools, 2495 as MCP resources, 201 as HTTP operations. Every one of those surfaces is rendered from the same rows, so an operation cannot exist in the API and be missing from the OpenAPI document, and a tool cannot appear over MCP that the registry does not know about. There is a gate that regenerates everything and fails if the result differs from what is committed.
cs: Registr je ta část, která se sama zaplatí. Každá operace je deklarována jednou, v Rustu, se svou identitou, efektem a expozicí. V době sestavení této stránky registr drží 2646 schopností: 196 z nich je vystaveno jako nástroje MCP, 2495 jako zdroje MCP, 201 jako operace HTTP. Každý z těchto povrchů se vykresluje ze stejných řádků, takže operace nemůže existovat v API a chybět v dokumentu OpenAPI a nástroj se nemůže objevit přes MCP, aniž by ho registr znal. Existuje kontrola, která vše znovu vygeneruje a selže, pokud se výsledek liší od toho, co je commitnuto.

en: <t1/> reads the workflow and the model and holds one to the other: the triggers, the absence of a path filter and of any pull-request trigger, the permissions, the concurrency group, the bounds, and the order of the three commands. It then takes the steps' own scripts out of the workflow and runs them against a scripted adapter and a local remote: without the executable none of them reaches the adapter, with drift owed the tip is applied, and a checkout the trunk has moved past applies nothing. Poté vyjme skripty jednotlivých kroků z workflow a spustí je proti skriptovanému adaptéru a lokálnímu remote: bez spustitelného souboru se k adaptéru nedostane žádný, při dlužném driftu se aplikuje špička a checkout, který trunk předběhl, neaplikuje nic.
